330|        instances=$(read_instances) || return "$?"
331|        jq -e --arg name "$SYSTEM_NAME" --arg pool "$SYSTEM_STORAGE" --arg status "$status" --arg uuid "$native_uuid" --arg op "$OPERATION_ID" '
332|            [.[]|select(.name==$name)] | select(length==1) | .[0] |
333|            .type=="container" and .status==$status and .profiles==[] and
334|            .config["volatile.uuid"]==$uuid and .config["user.opdbus.creation_operation"]==$op and
335|            .config["security.privileged"]=="false" and .config["security.nesting"]=="false" and
336|            .config["boot.autostart"]=="false" and
337|            .devices.root.type=="disk" and .devices.root.path=="/" and .devices.root.pool==$pool
338|        ' <<<"$instances" >/dev/null
339|    }
340|    instance_list=$(read_instances) || die 'assigned instance readback failed'
341|    state=$(jq -er --arg name "$SYSTEM_NAME" '[.[]|select(.name==$name)]|select(length==1)|.[0].status' <<<"$instance_list") || die 'assigned instance missing or ambiguous'
342|    case "$state" in
343|        Stopped) verify_instance Stopped || die 'created instance state differs; reconcile retained candidate' ;;
344|        Running)
345|            [[ $NO_START != true && $(jq -r .replayed <<<"$created") == true ]] || die 'unexpected running candidate; no lifecycle mutation performed'

347|            ;;
348|        *) die 'unsupported assigned instance state; reconcile retained candidate' ;;
349|    esac
350|    if [[ $NO_START != true && $state == Stopped ]]; then
351|        # A retained start intent is uncertain, not permission to issue another
352|        # start. A Running readback above can finish it without a mutation.
353|        jq -e '.start_requested!=true' "$intent" >/dev/null || die 'retained start intent is not running; inspect before explicit recovery'
354|        tmp=$(mktemp "$directory/.start.XXXXXX")
355|        jq '.start_requested=true' "$intent" > "$tmp"
356|        sync -f "$tmp"; mv -T "$tmp" "$intent"; sync -f "$directory"
357|        start_args=$(jq -cn --arg name "$SYSTEM_NAME" '{name:$name}')
358|        started=$(incus_call start_instance "$start_args") || die 'start failed or outcome uncertain; inspect existing instance before retrying'
359|        jq -e --arg name "$SYSTEM_NAME" '.name==$name and .state=="Running"' <<<"$started" >/dev/null || die 'start receipt differs'
360|        verify_instance Running || die 'running instance readback differs'
361|    fi
362|    printf 'Standalone container %s: mounted Incus receipts and native state verified; grants unchanged.\n' "$SYSTEM_NAME"
363|)
364|

366|    if [[ $IMAGE_OVERRIDDEN == false ]]; then IMAGE=$SYSTEM_IMAGE; fi
367|    provision_system_container; exit 0
368|fi

{"content":"1|#!/usr/bin/env bash
2|# Invoke one plugin method through the supported same-handle mounted client.
3|# The mount must already be bound to the caller's identity
4|# (e.g. /run/mounts/3tchedFS + /run/opdbus/lungs/lungs.sock).
5|#
6|# Capability grants and op-grants-materializer are not exposed here; durable policy
7|# stays under /etc/opdbus/local/ with owner-approved deltas only.
8|#
9|# Usage:
10|#   deploy/scripts/3tchedfs-invoke.sh <plugin> <method> [json-args] [--confirm-side-effects]
11|#   OP_3TCHEDFS_MOUNT=/run/mounts/3tchedFS deploy/scripts/3tchedfs-invoke.sh tched_router config_get '{"path":"agents.dashboard.model_provider"}'
12|set -euo pipefail
13|
14|die() { echo "3tchedfs-invoke: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
15|
16|MOUNT="${OP_3TCHEDFS_MOUNT:-/run/mounts/3tchedFS}"
17|CLIENT="${THREETCHED_FS:-/usr/local/libexec/op-dbus/bin/3tched-fs}"
18|PLUGIN="${1:?plugin id}"
19|METHOD="${2:?method name}"
20|shift 2
21|ARGS='{}'
22|if [[ $# -gt 0 && $1 != --confirm-side-effects ]]; then ARGS=$1; shift; fi
23|options=()
24|if [[ ${1:-} == --confirm-side-effects ]]; then options+=(--confirm-side-effects); shift; fi
25|[[ $# == 0 ]] || die 'pass one JSON argument and optional --confirm-side-effects'
26|[[ $PLUGIN =~ ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$ && $METHOD =~ ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$ ]] || die 'unsafe plugin or method name'
27|[[ -x $CLIENT ]] || die "mounted client absent: $CLIENT"
28|if [[ -n ${OP_3TCHEDFS_EXPECTED_SESSION:-} ]]; then
29|  options+=(--expected-session "$OP_3TCHEDFS_EXPECTED_SESSION")
30|fi
31|
32|[[ -f "$MOUNT/.3tchedfs.json" ]] || die "not a 3tchedFS root: $MOUNT"
33|case "$(findmnt -n -o FSTYPE -T "$MOUNT" 2>/dev/null || true)" in
34|  fuse|fuse.3tchedFS) ;;
35|  *) die "namespace is not a fuse 3tchedFS mount: $MOUNT" ;;
36|esac
37|
38|OP="$MOUNT/plugins/$PLUGIN/operations/$METHOD"
39|[[ -d "$OP" ]] || die "operation absent: $PLUGIN/$METHOD"
40|[[ -f "$OP/input.schema.json" ]] || die "missing input schema: $OP"
41|
42|if ! printf '%s' "$ARGS" | jq -e . >/dev/null 2>&1; then
43|  die "json-args must be valid JSON"
44|fi
45|
46|# invoke validates the sealed schema and pinned mount, fsyncs and reads the
47|# receipt on the same descriptor. Preserve its diagnostic and exit status;
48|# never retry an uncertain mutation or fall back to a different transport.
49|exec "$CLIENT" invoke --mount "$MOUNT" "${options[@]}" --args "$ARGS" \

{"content":"1|# Network Operations
2|
3|This page describes **how networking is supposed to work on the current Artix/runit host**, and points at the live inventory when the tree and the machine disagree.
4|
5|For a dated, command-verified snapshot of interfaces, Incus devices, listeners, xray SNI, and mesh forwarders, see:
6|
7|**[Host socket & network topology (live)](host-socket-topology-live.md)**
8|
9|Re-verify that file against the host before topology-changing work (new proxies, prom/graf exposure, socket migrations).
10|
11|## Agent rules and owner decisions (moved from AGENTS.md, 2026-10-14)
12|
13|Read this section before any network, Xray, WARP, decoy, OVS or firewall work.
14|AGENTS.md now only points here.
15|
16|**Partial restoration (2026-10-16).** The native `decoy-admin-reverse-ssh`
17|runit service is restored on the Devuan host using the existing
18|`/home/jeremy/.ssh/decoy_key` and strict host-key checking. The decoy publishes
19|`10.0.0.1:2222` bound to `wg-opdbus`, forwarding to its loopback reverse endpoint;
20|the tunnel terminates at the host's loopback SSH listener. WireGuard terminates
21|only on the decoy, never on this host. A fresh authenticated reverse connection
22|returned `jeremy` on `3tched` and matched the host's authoritative ED25519 key.
23|The external WireGuard-client leg was not exercised from this session.
24|
25|The target layout is eth0 as OVS uplink, pub0 for public addressing (not
26|administrative SSH), two IPv4 addresses on `rtly-lungs` including 10.0.0.2,
27|and three service aliases on ovsbr0 for EMQX, OpenFlow and Qdrant. OVS packages
28|are installed, but no bridge/address/route ownership cutover has occurred.
29|NetworkManager remains active until a protected transfer; afterward it must
30|remain installed but disabled, for emergency recovery only.
31|
32|Owner requests stopping at the application-bridge prerequisite. The existing
33|uplink service waits for `opdbus-rundirs`, which requires `/usr/local/bin/opblob`
34|and a prepared persisted catalog; that executable is absent. This is an
35|application-catalog bootstrap dependency, not proof that the bridge daemon must
36|run to create OVS. Do not bypass it or claim the network cutover is deployed.
37|Public recovery SSH is still enabled: a proposed private-only cutover was
38|reverted when its rollback helper could not execute on the `noexec` `/run`
39|mount. Move forward only with an approved, functioning rollback mechanism.
40|
41|**Current status (2026-10-14).** The host moved from Artix to Devuan 6 (runit:
42|`/etc/sv/<svc>`, enabled via `/etc/runit/runsvdir/default`). Only `eth0`
43|(`188.68.58.237/22`, DHCP) is up; OVS, Incus, Xray and WARP are not installed yet.
44|Owner decision: the network lives on the **base system**, not in a golden release,
45|installed on a new machine by a network preinstall script that pulls these
46|sources from git. The rest of this page, including the GRE description below,
47|predates that move: GRE (`gre-decoy`) and `wgcf` were retired on 2026-10-04 (see
48|`deploy/runit/retired-services`), and `deploy/config/nftables.conf` says SSH
49|transport now uses `tun5`. Xray config/keys and the Xray Incus container are not
50|in git; the recovery disk keeps them under `received/271/root-271/`
51|(`etc/xray`, `var/lib/incus`, `etc/openvswitch`, `etc/nftables.conf`).
52|
53|**Network-critical services.** OVS, uplink, DHCP and the session bus require
54|deliberate operator action; a learning or inventory pass never restarts them.
55|
56|**Xray configuration policy — mandatory.** Xray's live config must exist only at
57|`/etc/xray/xray_config.json` inside the container. Never point Xray at
58|`/dev/shm/xray_config.json`, `/usr/local/etc/xray/config.json`, or any other
59|disk-backed live path. The static bootstrap config is materialized at boot; the
60|future model-generated generator replaces the same file atomically and reloads
61|through D-Bus. Models must not write or reload Xray directly.
62|
63|**Owner-confirmed network topology (2026-09-13).** There is no WireGuard on this
64|server. WireGuard terminates at the decoy; identity is transported by WARP.
65|WireGuard types, plugin declarations, credentials or historical configuration
66|paths in source do not establish a server WireGuard interface or a requirement to
67|install one. Classify those surfaces by their decoy/server role before proposing
68|implementation or retirement. An unwired `wgcf` method is not evidence that the
69|actual WARP identity transport is broken.
70|
71|**Owner decisions: decoy GRE, TLS and identity transport (2026-09-25; GRE since
72|retired).** The door stays `10.0.0.2:8090`: tonic with the internal `svc0`
73|certificate from the op-dbus local CA. The bridge no longer listens on
74|`127.0.0.1:8090` or `10.0.0.3:8090`, and it no longer serves a second browser
75|certificate. Browser-facing TLS terminates on the decoy at `10.0.0.1`. The decoy
76|mints the sealed identity blob, and WARP delivers it to the 8090 interceptor. The
77|oracle (OIA1) is the decoy's signed proof of the WireGuard peer, because
78|WireGuard exists only on the decoy. At the time, the decoy routed browser
79|traffic for `10.0.0.2` over `gre-host` with no WARP route in either main routing
80|table. The `gre-decoy` tunnel joined decoy and host: outer `188.68.58.237` ↔
81|`129.80.64.127`, inner `192.168.255.1/30` plus `10.0.0.2/32`, with `10.0.0.1` and
82|the WireGuard clients `10.0.0.5`–`10.0.0.7` routed via `192.168.255.2`. GRE
83|routing replaced NAT on that path: nftables is the firewall only, never a router,
84|so do not add DNAT, SNAT or masquerade for it. GRE is not encrypted, so anything
85|crossing it that is not TLS is readable on the path. MQTT stays on `10.0.0.3`,
86|aliased on `ovsbr0` beside the OpenFlow address `10.200.0.1`. Xray runs in its
87|container. op-web's page address is `http://10.0.0.4:8080`: plain HTTP outside
88|the TLS zone, with `10.0.0.4/32` on `gre-decoy` and routed from the decoy over
89|`gre-host`. The decoy issuer
90|(`/etc/systemd/system/op-decoy-issuer.service.d/browser-auth.conf` on the decoy,
91|not in this repo) hands out the IP door `https://10.0.0.2:8090` and allows the
92|`10.0.0.4` and `10.0.0.2` page origins; no domain name points browsers at the
93|decoy. Open on 2026-09-25: how the decoy-minted oracle reaches the interceptor
94|(the owner's direction then was over GRE). Until that lands, the deployed page
95|fetches OIA1 from `http://10.0.0.1:51888/identity/self`, and the door rejects a
96|request that carries no credential.
97|
98|## Model in one paragraph
99|
100|One OVS bridge (`ovsbr0`) carries the private fabric. Physical uplink (`eth0`) is enslaved and unaddressed; host L3 lives on OVS internal ports **`pub0`** (public) and **`svc0`** (`10.200.0.2/24`). The **xray** container is the only instance with a NIC on the bridge (`10.200.0.1`). WireGuard mesh interface **`3tched`** (`100.69.0.254/16`) is separate L3 and must never be routed via `ovsbr0`.
101|
102|**Shared socket fabric:** `op-grpc-bridge` dual-listens on host UDS `/run/opdbus/grpc.sock` and shared container UDS `/run/ghostbridge/container.sock` (same gRPC routes). NIC-less containers bind-mount `/run/ghostbridge`. Some services still use Incus TCP proxies / mesh `fwd-*` (migration is incremental).
103|
104|**OpenFlow** (`op-of-controller` on `127.0.0.1:6653`) is intentionally NORMAL/standalone today — reserved for **future tag routing**, not a current blocker for the socket fabric.
105|
106|## Boot order (runit)
107|
108|```text
109|opdbus-rundirs
110|  → uplink-dhcp
111|  → ovsdb-server → ovs-vswitchd
112|  → ovsbr0-uplink → ovsbr0-addr → ovsbr0-svc-addr
113|  → op-of-controller
114|  → wg-3tched
115|  → op-grpc-bridge (cognitive in process) / op-web
116|```
117|
118|Config: `/etc/op-dbus/network.conf`  
119|Helpers: `/usr/local/libexec/3tched/*-up`
120|
121|## Public path
122|
123|Client DNS (NextDNS) → Oracle decoy → WireGuard mesh → host `fwd-8444` → xray SNI on `10.200.0.1:8444` → host services on `10.200.0.2` (dashboard/registration → `:8080`, assistant gRPC → `:8090`, etc.). Live rules: `/dev/shm/xray_config.json` only.
124|
125|## Attachment modes (summary)
126|
127|| Pattern | Used by (live) |
128|| --- | --- |
129|| Bridged NIC on `ovsbr0` | `xray` only |
130|| Shared UDS `/run/ghostbridge/container.sock` | bridge + CT mounts (`assistant`, `qdrant`) |
131|| Incus `proxy` TCP | `mail-3tched`, `netmaker`, `qdrant`, `cozo` |
132|| Mesh `tcpfwd.py` (`fwd-*`) | side channels into xray/host |
133|| Host UDS `/run/opdbus/grpc.sock` | host gRPC clients, session bus |
134|
135|## Do / don't
136|
137|- **Do** check `sudo incus config device show <name>` before assuming UDS-only or proxy-only.
138|- **Do** keep mesh routes on `3tched`; strip accidental `100.69.0.0/16` via `ovsbr0`.
139|- **Do** treat the [Netmaker ACL helper](host-socket-topology-live.md#break-glass-netmaker-acl-recovery) as break-glass recovery; it enables wildcard all-node traffic and bypasses the normal D-Bus path.
140|- **Do not** put `10.200.0.1` on the host.
141|- **Do not** point live xray at `/etc/xray/config.json`.
142|- **Do not** expose Prometheus/Grafana from the netmaker container until the live topology doc is current and the path (mesh vs SNI vs loopback) is chosen.
143|
144|## Stale references
145|
146|Older address tables and dinit/ens3 socket-port writeups under `docs/network-address-table.md` and `docs/operations/ghostbridge-incus-ovs-architecture.md` describe previous hosts or intent. Prefer the live topology snapshot and this page for the 2026-07 Artix/runit host.","total_lines":146,"file_size":9175,"truncated":false,"is_binary":false,"is_image":false,"not_found":false}
